reading.body:
SJC11 publishes 73,000 square feet of technical space but no power consumption figure, making its actual AI hosting capacity unknowable from available information.

Floor area alone does not signal compute density. A facility can house vastly different workload types at vastly different power densities per square foot depending on tenant mix and design. The 73,000 square feet is a measure of physical footprint, not of the megawatts that determine how many GPUs or accelerators the building can run. Without the power figure, the space tells you only that the facility exists at material scale in Santa Clara County, not whether it serves AI training or other workload categories.

The six certifications listed qualify SJC11 for regulated workloads: financial services under PCI DSS, healthcare under HIPAA, and general operational audits under SOC 2 Type 2 and SSAE 18. LEED and Green Globes attest to environmental design and operations, not to infrastructure for high-density compute. None of these certifications exist for GPU-scale AI training, because compliance categories do not yet track that workload class.

California has 103 mapped data center facilities in this dataset, but only five publish megawatt figures, totaling 170 MW across those five. SJC11 falls outside that published group. Within Santa Clara County's concentration of compute infrastructure, this is a mid-scale colocation facility whose relevance to AI depends on power specifications the operator has chosen not to disclose.
